messages:
deploybot: Release pipeline for service-x v1.2.3 paused: SBOM provenance mismatch detected (artifact signed but cosign verification failed). link: https://ci.internal/runs/4577 :rotating_light:
marco (release-manager): ack. pausing rollout. can someone grab the cosign output and the build provenance? we need evidence to unblock. :eyes:
oliver (sec-eng): grabbing logs now. quick note — the signature exists but claims a different builder id than our repo. could be rebase build or sys image change.
oliver (sec-eng): ```
$ cosign verify --key ksm://projects/infra/keys/cosign service-x:1.2.3
error: signature verification failed: signature payload mismatch: "Rekor index entry does not match expected builder id"
```
marco (release-manager): thanks. tanya / legal — is that an immediate hard block or do we accept manual attestation?
tanya (security): we need cryptographic proof of provenance for prod releases. if cosign fails we need either: 1) a signed attestation from build-team matching the SHA256 and repo commit, or 2) re-run the build in our controlled builder and re-sign. no quick exceptions unless it's time-critical and SLA-approved.
nana (qa): we also have failing e2e flakes in the canary run (non-deterministic timeout). not comfortable continuing without a scoped rerun.
legal-bot: license-scan: no new license flags. vulnerability-scan: low-sev transitive in test deps only. compliance-hold: off.
marco (release-manager): proposed path: revert canary (stop rollout), request build-team to produce signed attestation or re-run pipeline in prod-builder, attach cosign output + build URL, then re-trigger canary during next change window (tomorrow 02:00-04:00 UTC). any objections?
oliver (sec-eng): +1 to attestation. if build-team can provide the signed statement with KMS key id and exact digest we can fast-track verification. otherwise we re-run. also request Rekor proof.
tanya (security): please include the Rekor entry and the PGP/KMS key fingerprint. without Rekor we don't consider it provenance-complete.
nana (qa): tagging flaky test owners @qa-team — we can gate the canary to skip the flaky suite and do smoke-only if security sponsors re-run. else hold.
deploybot: pipeline run https://ci.internal/runs/4577 kept, new run queued as https://ci.internal/runs/4580 (prod-builder). status: paused -> manual_approval_required.
marco (release-manager): I'll message build-team now. if we get attestation before the change window we can still do a scoped canary (5% traffic) with manual rollback hooks. otherwise hold for re-run.
oliver (sec-eng): one more ask — if they supply attestation, we need them to attest the exact Docker manifest digest and the git commit SHA. cookie-cutter text below they can sign:
```
I attest that docker manifest sha256:abc123... corresponds to git commit 9f8e7d and was produced by the prod-builder at builder-host-02. Signed with KMS key projects/infra/keys/cosign.
```
marco (release-manager): noted. pinging @build-team.
build-team (via deploybot): build-team acknowledged. will provide attestation or re-run within 90m.
marco (release-manager): thanks. interim decision: HOLD release until attestation OR successful prod-builder re-run + cosign verify + Rekor proof. if attestation arrives with all fields we'll allow a limited canary in the current change window with QA smoke and manual approval. please react with :thumbsup: if you agree.
oliver (sec-eng): :thumbsup:
tanya (security): :thumbsup:
nana (qa): :thumbsup:
marco (release-manager): logging decision in release notes draft and tagging incident for traceability. will update thread when we have artifacts.
deploybot: note: manual_approval_required -> awaiting artifacts.
